130  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

I attended Savoy College from 1886 to 1889. I could not speak English at all when I started to school, but while I attended school I mixed, mingled, moved my young family westward, first to Illinois, thence to southwestern Missouri, where Thomas J. Chenoweth had settled, and soon picked up their language. The teachers during that time were George W. Chenoweth, and other arts graduates. When I left this school after it burned I went to Spencer Academy near Hugo, Oklahoma. I became interpreter for the United States Court and doorkeeper for the Chickasaw Legislature. I can not remember the rest of the teachers. When I left this school after it burned I went to Spencer Academy near Hugo, Oklahoma. I became interpreter for the United States Court and doorkeeper for the Choctaw court by Judge Easton. The deed was so much defaced as to be unreadable. I was a deputy United States Marshal under R. P. Taylor. I became a deputy sheriff under A. Phillips in Bryan County, Oklahoma.

During all of my experience as a peace officer, both for the Choctaw Nation and the State of Oklahoma, I have always been able to take care of myself in any situation that might arise. The training I received while I was in an Oklahoma level joint and some one knew that I could not speak or write the English language was of great value to me. I got along very well without a scratch with the exception of several pistol-shot wounds, from two different men. I have always tried to uphold the law and relieve the laws of our country.

sell, who was so much help to me when I attended school at Savoy, Texas.*

*Personal letter from Mr. Frank Anderson, Durant, Oklahoma, August 4, 1938.
notes: Page 130 of printed text. Continuation and conclusion of Frank Anderson's personal letter about Savoy College. Footnote references personal letter dated August 4, 1938.
